notes_for_editor: Heights disagree: the 1938 state report (via Forest Lookouts) gives 99 ft 9 in for the 1937 tower; Jerry Tilley says the 1968 move added 20 ft, and no source gives the post-move height, so none is recorded. The Legeros page gives the tower as 99 ft but its height glyph does not survive text extraction, so it is not quoted. The Legeros Fire Line Facebook post and an ncfiretowers Instagram post (2020, says 100 ft) were seen only as search snippets and are not cited. WRAL (May 2023) reports that the Forest Service removed the bottom steps to stop people climbing and says the tower is one to look at, not touch; no source gives formal public-access rules for the Howard Road site. WRAL (May 2023) and the Legeros history (January 2017) disagree on the house below the tower (Forest Service office versus private residence); the story reports both. Current condition is not confirmed. The record's coordinates (35.88916, -78.68333) were not checked against a source with coordinates. The separate record us-nc-bayleaf-old (EZ 5204, 35.90527, -78.65361) may be the original Six Forks Road site; not verified.
